scores.critique: Best validation protocol of the four: point-in-time bulk-EOD universe rebuilt per date, delisting penalty applied against the position, purged/embargoed expanding walk-forward, a deliberately small prior-based feature set, and a real sanity battery (shuffle-label, extra-lag, decile monotonicity). Honest Sharpe bands. Sharpest flaws: (1) XSR feature 4 depends on an EODHD symbol-list 'sector field' that does not exist — sector data lives in the 403'd fundamentals API, so this is wishful data; (2) the train-on-true-close / trade-at-15:45-provisional-features mismatch is a systematic live-vs-backtest wedge on a reversal signal where the final 15 minutes carry most of the signal — 'document it as noise' is not a mitigation, it needs a quantified ablation; (3) NRV builds training labels from EODHD historical news whose timestamps are crawl-time (the news-llm design correctly bans that corpus as a timestamp source) — switch to Alpaca news REST; (4) no fractional shorting means the 20-name short book at ~$340/name is chunky whole-share rounding with unmodeled tracking error; (5) ONX is pre-admitted near-zero. KEEP: D0/D1 infrastructure, XSR core with hysteresis turnover control, the sanity battery, the overnight gross ≤1.9x Reg-T guard.

Best news-data discipline anywhere in the packet: byte-identical Alpaca REST backtest corpus vs live websocket, created_at-only timestamp law with +5s latency and ≥60s entry delay, entity-masking contamination audit with FinBERT-only ablation floor, randomized-sentiment null-Sharpe benchmark, lag-cliff test. But the edge class itself is the most heavily arbitraged in systematic trading and the design admits seconds-latency vs millisecond professionals — alpha probability is the packet's lowest. Understated costs: the rule gate (materiality ≥ 6) requires Gemini scores on the ENTIRE story corpus (millions of stories 2016-present), not just the 30-60k gated events; Sleeve C additionally needs 1-2M embeddings — the LLM pipeline bill and wall-clock are underestimated by an order of magnitude. The 500-story masking audit is statistically underpowered to detect moderate contamination. Sleeve C duplicates the no-news reversal trade built in two other designs, and its short leg is structurally flattered by paper fills (no borrow, no buy-ins). KEEP: §0.3 timestamp law, the contamination protocol, and the null-benchmark methodology as system-wide standards.

Sleeve 1 (ETF intraday momentum) is the single best first deployment in the entire packet: fixed 27-ETF universe with zero survivorship issues, auction fills via opg/cls TIF (SIP prints, sidestepping IEX entirely), a deliberately tiny meta-filter with the rule-only baseline reported separately, and a pre-registered 2022-2025-positive-at-2x-costs gate — live on paper in ~2 weeks. Honest that the per-trade edge is a razor-thin 2-4bps net on a post-publication anomaly; alpha is modest but the overfit surface is the smallest of any sleeve. Sleeve 2's opening-window spread modeling (Corwin-Schultz, 2x-cost stress gate) is the most honest cost treatment of any gap design. Hard feasibility break in Sleeve 3: streaming IEX bars for 600 symbols exceeds Alpaca free-tier websocket symbol limits (~30 symbols) — the claim 'within free-tier limits' is wrong as written; combined with self-assessed 40-50% death probability and REST-vs-websocket timestamp fiction, Sleeve 3 dies. Its shadow-mode latency-reconciliation tooling, however, is the best single idea in the packet and must survive as shared infrastructure. Sleeve 2 redundantly duplicates gap sleeves in two other designs — merge, don't triplicate.

Part B is the best portfolio plumbing of the four — intent-based OMS with netting and internal crossing, attribution ledger in BigQuery, hard pre-trade risk limits, drawdown kill ladder, fail-closed data-quality gates matching the owner's existing bot philosophy — and the correlation-to-sector-ETF assignment is the correct, actually-feasible answer to the 403'd fundamentals API. Sharpest flaws: (1) S1 signals at 17:30 but enters t+1 09:40, forfeiting the overnight portion of short-term reversal where much of the documented capture concentrates — the expected-capture assumption (25% reversion) is likely optimistic by construction and the design never tests close-entry vs open-entry; (2) the Isolation Forest gate is an unaudited researcher degree of freedom — no required ablation vs plain |resid_z|>2 gating, weekly refits on 60d windows are non-stationary and unreproducible without snapshot discipline; (3) S3's tradable rotation leg is alpha-free defensive beta (self-admitted Sharpe 0.3-0.6) that overlaps the owner's existing regime sleeve conceptually; (4) Hedge/exponentiated-gradient reweighting on 90d realized Sharpe is noise-chasing even clipped — equal-risk is the defensible choice for year one; (5) OMS-first sequencing means no live orders for ~5-6 weeks. KEEP: OMS/risk layer, sector-correlation mapping, HMM as overlay-only with its pre-registered +0.1-Sharpe gate.

kill_list: ONX overnight/intraday tilt (xs-ml-ranker Sleeve 3): pre-admitted net Sharpe -0.2 to +0.7 where the entire return is a bet against the spread cost model; 30 orders/day of churn plus concentrated overnight gap risk on longs for an expected-zero edge. Do not build, even at 2-3 days cost.

Intraday News-Shock Continuation (intraday-anomaly Sleeve 3) as designed: the 600-symbol IEX bar websocket exceeds Alpaca free-tier symbol subscription limits (~30 symbols), so the live trigger architecture is data-infeasible as written; combined with REST-vs-websocket timestamp fiction and a self-assessed 40-50% kill probability on the most-harvested signal class in systematic trading. Salvage only the shadow-mode reconciliation tooling.

HMM tradable rotation leg (anomaly-regime-meta S3 §2-5): defensive beta with regime timing, self-admitted Sharpe 0.3-0.6, conceptually duplicates the owner's existing Regime SSO sleeve. Keep the HMM as a risk overlay/monitor only.

Duplicate gap sleeves — news-llm-event Sleeve B and anomaly-regime-meta S2 as separate builds: three designs propose the same overnight-gap drift-vs-fade trade; building it three times triples data-snooping surface with zero orthogonal alpha. Merge into ONE gap engine (see keep list).

Stale/Soft News Fade (news-llm-event Sleeve C) as a standalone sleeve: decayed 15-year-old Tetlock effect, short leg structurally flattered by paper fills (no borrow costs or buy-ins), and a 1-2M-story embedding backfill bill for a Sharpe 0.3-0.8 sleeve that duplicates the no-news reversal trade in two other designs. Fold its novelty-embedding feature into the single merged reversal sleeve instead.

XSR feature 4 sector dependency on the 'EODHD symbol list sector field' (xs-ml-ranker §3): that field does not exist outside the 403'd fundamentals API — wishful data. Replace with anomaly-regime-meta's correlation-to-sector-ETF assignment.

EODHD historical news as a timestamp-bearing training source (xs-ml-ranker NRV §3-4): EODHD news timestamps are crawl-time/date-only per the news-llm design's own audit; training reversion labels on them is a built-in leakage vector. All timestamped news labels must come from Alpaca/Benzinga REST; EODHD news is count/confirmation features only.

Hedge/exponentiated-gradient adaptive sleeve reweighting (anomaly-regime-meta B1) in the first 6 months of live paper: 90-day realized Sharpe is mostly noise; even clipped, this is noise-chasing with extra machinery. Run equal-risk-contribution until >=6 months of live sleeve PnL exists, then revisit.

NRV as a trained ML meta-model in v1 (xs-ml-ranker Sleeve 2 §4): a few thousand events against dozens of features is small-sample overfit territory the design itself flags. Ship the rule-based no-news fade core first (it must be profitable standalone per the design's own acceptance rule); add the meta-filter only after the rule survives live paper.
keep_list: D0 point-in-time universe layer (xs-ml-ranker): EODHD bulk-EOD historical snapshots to BigQuery, universe rebuilt per backtest date, conservative delisting penalty applied against the position, raw snapshots stored immutably (never re-downloaded over old partitions). This is the survivorship-bias foundation every sleeve depends on.

XSR core sleeve (xs-ml-ranker Sleeve 1): LightGBM cross-sectional ranker on the frozen ~24 prior-based features, within-date rank transforms of features and labels, purged/embargoed expanding-window walk-forward with monthly retrain, hysteresis-based turnover control (exit below 70th percentile, enter above 90th).

Deployment sanity battery as a system-wide gate (xs-ml-ranker §7 + intraday-anomaly gates): shuffle-label test, extra-lag/lag-cliff test, decile monotonicity, per-subperiod survival, AND the 2x-cost stress gate — every sleeve must pass all of these pre-registered, or it does not deploy.

ETF Intraday Momentum sleeve (intraday-anomaly Sleeve 1), built and deployed FIRST: fixed 27-ETF universe, opg/cls auction orders for SIP-print fills, tiny meta-filter with rule-only baseline always reported separately, pre-registered 2022-2025-positive-at-2x-costs go/no-go gate. Fastest honest path to live paper orders (~2 weeks).

Timestamp-honesty law (news-llm-event §0.3) as system-wide standard: created_at only (never updated_at), +5s processing latency on all historical events, earliest fill >=60s after signal, Alpaca news REST as the ONLY timestamp-bearing news corpus, EODHD news demoted to count/confirmation features.

LLM contamination protocol (news-llm-event §0.2): entity masking in all historical Gemini prompts, masked-vs-unmasked predictive audit (expand beyond 500 stories), FinBERT-only ablation as the floor estimate, prompt version-pinning with classifications cached in BigQuery for reproducibility.

ONE merged overnight-gap sleeve combining the best of the three proposals: point-in-time top-600 universe and opening-window spread cost model (intraday-anomaly Sleeve 2), OPG auction entry with decision-noise simulation and fail-closed news classifier (anomaly-regime-meta S2), never-fade blacklist for M&A/FDA/offering/guidance-surprise events (news-llm-event Sleeve B §9), 2x-cost deployment gate.

ONE merged no-news residual-reversal sleeve: sector-hedged resid_z construction with correlation-to-sector-ETF assignment (anomaly-regime-meta S1), same-day ~15:50 entry to capture overnight reversion (xs-ml-ranker NRV timing — not next-morning 09:40 entry), hard fail-closed news blocklist via Gemini keyword classes, rule-based core first with meta-filter added only after live validation.

Part B OMS and risk layer (anomaly-regime-meta): sleeves write intents, OMS nets orders with attribution ledger, hard pre-trade limits (gross/net/per-name/per-sector), drawdown kill ladder (-8% halve, -12% flat+halt), 10-minute position reconciler vs Alpaca, fail-closed data-staleness gates, QNT- client_order_id lineage isolating the shared paper account.

HMM regime monitor as overlay-only (anomaly-regime-meta S3) with its pre-registered gate: causal filtered decoding only, hysteresis band, and it must improve the reversal sleeve's net Sharpe by >=0.1 in the 2016+ sample or it ships as monitoring-only.

Shadow-mode latency reconciliation tooling (intraday-anomaly Sleeve 3 step 5): log live websocket arrival times vs REST timestamps for identical stories and re-run backtests with the measured latency distribution — mandatory infrastructure gate before ANY news-latency-sensitive sleeve deploys, even though the sleeve it was designed for is killed.
Overnight Reg-T guard (xs-ml-ranker combined-system section): buying-power check enforcing gross <=1.9x overnight across all sleeves, enforced in the OMS pre-trade layer.

Pre-registered per-sleeve kill criteria written before backtests run (all four designs converge on this): trailing live-vs-backtest hit-rate triggers, 'reported dead, not tuned until green', and no reinstatement without human review.

scores.critique: Sharpest criticism: it smuggles in a sector data dependency that does not exist in the entitlements — features 4 (`ret_5d_resid` vs 'EODHD symbol list sector field') and the 30%-per-sector risk cap require sector classification, which on EODHD lives in the fundamentals API (confirmed 403); the symbol list endpoint has no sector field. As written, Sleeve 1 cannot be built; it needs Design 4's correlation-to-sector-ETF assignment transplanted in. Second: the 15:45-provisional-features vs trained-on-true-closes mismatch is waved off as 'noise' but reversal signals at 5d horizon are exactly where a 10-min price gap flips marginal ranks — quantify it, don't document it. Third: Sleeve 3 (ONX) self-assesses Sharpe −0.2 to +0.7 yet forces XSR to degross from 1.5x to 1.3x to fit Reg-T overnight — paying certain opportunity cost for an expected-zero sleeve. What to keep: D0 is the best point-in-time universe design of the four (bulk-EOD snapshots stored raw, asymmetric delisting penalty, conservative-against-us), the sanity battery (shuffle-label, extra-lag, decile monotonicity) is exactly right, and the hysteresis turnover control plus the short-side-attribution rejection rule (>60% of alpha from short small-caps ⇒ reject) show real production instincts.

Sharpest criticism: feasibility is dragged down by scope, and one sleeve contradicts its own cost model. Sleeve C's prerequisite is embedding ~1–2M historical stories — a multi-day pipeline and the long pole of the whole design — to enable a sleeve it itself rates at net Sharpe 0.3–0.8; compute novelty on-the-fly for triggered candidates only (trailing 5d window per symbol) and the backfill shrinks 100x. Sleeve B's fade leg claims alpha in price ≥ $3 / ADV ≥ $5M names, but §0.4 prices that bucket at 12bps half-spread or excludes it outright — the 'less arbitraged' fade universe is less arbitraged because it is untradeable at these entitlements. Entity masking for Gemini contamination is the right idea but overrated as a fix: Flash-class models identify '[COMPANY], the largest EV maker' trivially; the FinBERT-only ablation floor is the real safeguard and should be the pre-registered headline number. What to keep: this design's §0.3 timestamp-honesty rules (created_at only, +5s processing latency, first-full-minute-bar-≥60s fills, EODHD news never defines entry times) and the masked/unmasked contamination audit are the best leakage discipline in the entire set and should become house law for every news sleeve regardless of whose design wins. Sleeve A's meta-labeling structure (frozen rule gate + LightGBM only as filter) is the correct way to spend limited event samples.

Sharpest criticism: Sleeve 3 is a 10–15 day build for a signal the author assigns 40–50% prior probability of death, sitting at the most-harvested point in the systematic space (intraday news drift on $50M+ ADV names at T+5min); the shadow-mode gate is admirable but the expected value of the build is near zero — infrastructure reuse is the only honest justification and it's thin. Also note the websocket fine print: verified against Alpaca docs, the Basic plan's 30-symbol cap applies to trades/quotes channels while the minute-bar channel is unlimited — so the 600-symbol bar stream is legitimate, but marketable-limit pegging ('IEX last + 10bps') for bursty candidate sets must use REST latest-quote batches, not streamed quotes; the design doesn't say this and should. What to keep: Sleeve 1 is the single best sleeve across all four documents — public-literature anomaly, fixed no-survivorship universe, tiny meta-model on top of a rule that trades without ML, and above all the auction-execution doctrine (opg/cls orders fill at official SIP auction prints, structurally sidestepping the IEX-quality problem that plagues every other design). The ±30s/±5bps jitter test as a design-review gate, opening-window (not daily-average) spread estimation via Corwin–Schultz, 2x-cost deployment gates, and pre-registered go/no-go criteria are institutional-grade. Fastest credible path to live paper orders (~2 weeks) of any design.

Sharpest criticism: it builds the cathedral before the congregation exists — 8–12 days of OMS with intent-netting, internal crossing at IEX mid, and pro-rata fill attribution, plus a Hedge/exponentiated-gradient allocation overlay, all before a single sleeve has proven live edge; the Hedge overlay reweights on 90d realized Sharpe, which at these Sharpe levels is ~90% noise even with the [0.5, 1.8] clip, and the design half-admits this. S2's trigger depends on a 09:26–09:28 IEX pre-open quote midpoint across ~500 names — IEX pre-open books are thin and stale, the 30-symbol quote-stream cap forces REST sweeps, and even with the staleness gate and decision-noise backtest the realistic outcome is that most mornings produce zero tradeable signals (the design calls that 'correct behavior', but then the sleeve's PnL rests on ~30 mornings/yr — fragile). The Isolation Forest layer in S1 is an unfalsifiable gate: no ablation is specified to show iforest-gating beats plain |resid_z| ranking. What to keep: the correlation-based sector-ETF assignment (refreshed monthly) is the correct, entitlement-clean answer to the missing fundamentals API and should be transplanted into any cross-sectional sleeve; S3's causally-decoded HMM with hysteresis and the ships-as-monitoring-unless-it-adds-0.1-Sharpe rule is exactly how regime overlays should be gated; the B3 hard risk table (fail-closed data-quality gates, drawdown ladder, per-sleeve kill rules) and the candidates-logged-whether-traded-or-not audit trail are the best risk/observability spec of the four.

kill_list: Design 1 Sleeve 3 (ONX overnight tilt): self-assessed net Sharpe −0.2 to +0.7 straddling zero, effect heavily decayed post-2015, cost model IS the strategy (8bps/day RT vs 5–15bps gross), and it forces the core XSR sleeve to degross from 1.5x to 1.3x to fit Reg-T overnight limits — a certain cost paid for an expected-zero payoff. Do not build.

Design 1's sector features as specced (ret_5d_resid + 30% sector cap via 'EODHD symbol list sector field'): the data does not exist in the entitlements — sector requires the fundamentals API, which is 403. Kill the specced implementation; if the XSR sleeve is built, it must use Design 4's correlation-to-sector-ETF assignment instead.

Design 3 Sleeve 3 (intraday news-shock continuation): 10–15 build days for a signal with author-assessed 40–50% kill probability at the most-arbitraged point in the news-alpha space; its residual edge claim rests on historical REST timestamps matching live websocket delivery, which the design itself doubts. At most revisit after the news infra exists for other reasons; do not build as a first-wave sleeve.

Two of the three duplicate gap sleeves — Design 2 Sleeve B and Design 4 S2: D2-B's fade-leg universe (price ≥ $3, ADV ≥ $5M) is untradeable under its own §0.4 cost model; D4-S2 depends on thin, stale IEX pre-open quotes across ~500 names (30-symbol quote-stream cap forces REST sweeps) and concentrates PnL in ~30 mornings/yr. Keep exactly one gap sleeve: Design 3 Sleeve 2 (09:35 entry, opening-window spread model, cls auction exits).

Two of the three duplicate no-news-fade sleeves — Design 1 Sleeve 2 (NRV) and Design 2 Sleeve C as standalone builds: same Chan-2003 effect built three times. Merge into one news-conditioned dislocation-fade sleeve (Design 4 S1's residual/candidate framing + Design 2's LLM materiality gate and timestamp rules).

Design 2 Sleeve C's full 1–2M-story embedding backfill as a prerequisite: multi-day pipeline gating a Sharpe 0.3–0.8 sleeve. Compute novelty on-the-fly over a trailing 5-day per-symbol window for triggered candidates only.

Design 4 B1 Hedge/exponentiated-gradient adaptive allocation: reweighting on 90d realized Sharpe is noise-chasing at these Sharpe levels regardless of the clip. Static equal-risk allocation until ≥1 year of live sleeve PnL exists; the design's own 'enable only after 60 live days' hedge is still too aggressive.

Design 4's full OMS (intent netting, internal crossing at IEX mid, pro-rata fill attribution) as a precondition for first trade: 8–12 engineering days of meta-layer before any edge is proven. Slim to: Firestore QNT- position ledger + pre-trade gross/net/per-name caps + drawdown kill ladder + reconciler. Netting/crossing only becomes relevant when ≥2 sleeves overlap in symbols, which the merged sleeve plan makes rare.

Design 4 S3's tradable leg (QQQ/IWM/RSP/IEF/GLD/BIL rotation): net Sharpe 0.3–0.6 defensive beta-timing that duplicates the account owner's existing regime-rotation strategies conceptually and adds nothing an ML-anomaly desk needs. Ship the HMM as monitoring/risk-overlay only, gated on the pre-registered +0.1-Sharpe improvement test.
keep_list: Design 3 Sleeve 1 (ETF intraday momentum, first-30-min → last-30-min, rule core + tiny LightGBM meta-filter): build FIRST — cleanest anomaly, no survivorship issue, 4–6 day build, deployable alone, live on paper within ~2 weeks.

Design 3's auction-execution doctrine: opg/cls orders fill at official SIP auction prints, structurally sidestepping IEX quote quality. Adopt as the default exit (and where applicable entry) mechanism for every sleeve in the final architecture.

Design 1 D0 point-in-time universe layer: EODHD bulk-EOD daily snapshots stored raw in BigQuery, universe rebuilt per historical date, asymmetric delisting penalty (conservative against the strategy), corporate-action screens. This is the shared foundation every cross-sectional sleeve stands on.

Design 2 §0.3 timestamp-honesty rules as house law for all news work: created_at only (never updated_at), +5s fixed processing latency, earliest fill = first full minute bar ≥ 60s post-signal, EODHD news never defines entry times, dedup by symbol+Jaccard.

Design 2 §0.2 LLM contamination protocol: entity-masked Gemini scoring with the masked-vs-unmasked audit, and — critically — the FinBERT-only ablation as the pre-registered floor estimate for any news sleeve's headline number.

Design 4's correlation-based sector assignment (each stock mapped to the sector ETF with highest 120d return correlation, refreshed monthly): the entitlement-clean substitute for the 403'd fundamentals API; transplant into every sleeve that needs sector hedging or sector caps.

One merged cross-sectional core sleeve: Design 1 Sleeve 1 (XSR LightGBM ranker — feature list, rank-transformed labels, purged expanding-window walk-forward, hysteresis turnover control, short-side-attribution rejection rule) with Design 4's sector assignment replacing the broken sector field.

One merged news-conditioned dislocation-fade sleeve: Design 4 S1's residual-dislocation candidate framing + Design 2's LLM materiality gate, timestamp rules, and reversal-factor-regression kill criterion (must show alpha over generic short-term reversal or die).
One gap sleeve: Design 3 Sleeve 2 (09:35 entry after opening range, opening-window Corwin–Schultz spread model, cls auction exit, 2x-cost deployment gate, short-side HTB attribution split).

Design 3's shadow-mode reconciliation gate as a pre-registered no-go criterion for anything latency-sensitive: 4 weeks logging live websocket arrival times vs historical REST timestamps before capital deployment.

Design 4 B3 risk table + fail-closed data-quality gates + candidates-logged-whether-traded-or-not audit trail (signals.candidates in BQ): the observability spec that makes live-vs-backtest drift measurable; adopt at the portfolio layer (slimmed OMS, per kill list).

Design 4 S3 HMM regime monitor as monitoring-only overlay: causal (filtered, never smoothed) decoding, hysteresis band, 2-day confirmation, stress-state validation against 2008/2011/2015/2018/2020/2022, and the pre-registered rule that it only gates sleeve sizing if it improves S1-class net Sharpe by ≥0.1.

The shared honesty framing common to all four designs: combined net Sharpe ~0.6–1.3, net CAGR ~8–20%, explicit refusal to represent 50%/yr as achievable at IEX/retail latency — this must survive verbatim into every report to the account owner.

scores.critique: The strongest core sleeve of the four. XSR (cross-sectional LightGBM on ~24 prior-backed price/volume features, point-in-time EODHD bulk universe, purged walk-forward, shuffle/lag/decile sanity battery) is exactly the right flagship: the data is verified-available, the feature set is deliberately small, the honesty about 5-15% net CAGR is correct, and the delisting-penalty treatment is more careful than most retail shops ever get. Sharpest criticisms: (1) Position granularity at $9k is worse than the doc admits — $340/position with whole-share shorts means any stock over ~$170 is 1-2 shares and the short book carries chunky residual net exposure; the ±5% net cap will bind constantly and the equal-weight assumption in the backtest will not match live. Backtest must simulate whole-share rounding, not footnote it. (2) The 15:45 provisional-feature vs trained-on-true-close mismatch is waved through as 'noise' — for a reversal-heavy model the last 15 minutes ARE signal; quantify the degradation before live, don't document it. (3) NRV trains its news-conditioning labels on EODHD historical news, whose timestamps the design itself admits are sometimes ingestion-time — that is a leak machine; design 2 solves this correctly with the Alpaca/Benzinga REST corpus, so NRV's concept should survive but its EODHD-timestamp implementation should not. (4) ONX is a self-confessed ~zero-EV sleeve built to inflate trade count; 30 orders/day of cost-equals-edge trading is activity theater, not irregularity exploitation. Keep: D0/D1 point-in-time infrastructure (best-articulated version across all four designs), XSR wholesale, the shared-account position-ledger discipline, the pre-registered live-IC de-risking rule.

The most methodologically sophisticated document, and the only one that gets the news-corpus problem right: backtesting on Alpaca REST Benzinga history (byte-identical to the live websocket) instead of EODHD crawl-time stamps is the single most important data decision in any news design, and the entity-masking + masked-vs-unmasked contamination audit is genuinely institutional-grade and rarely done anywhere. The timestamp-honesty rules (created_at only, +5s latency, first-bar-≥60s fills, lag-cliff test) should become house law. Sharpest criticisms: (1) Masking is not a cure — a memorized guidance number or FDA drug name identifies the company even with [COMPANY] substitution; the audit detects gross contamination but the residual is unmeasurable, so the FinBERT-only ablation must be treated as the deployable floor, not a footnote. (2) 20+ event types × materiality × sentiment × P-thresholds is a researcher-degrees-of-freedom minefield; 'taxonomy frozen before backtest' is asserted but unenforceable by one person — needs the null-distribution benchmark to be the binding gate, and it is (good). (3) Sleeve C is the weakest link: a 15-year-old, admittedly decayed Tetlock effect whose own pre-registered audit (alpha over generic reversal) it will probably fail, gated behind the single most expensive build item in all four documents (embedding backfill over ~1-2M stories). Kill it; if staleness matters it can be a cheap feature in the gap sleeve. (4) 2-6 trades/day from Sleeve A is on the low end of the 'very active' mandate; the design earns its place on quality, not activity. (5) ~30% self-assessed probability the whole thing is flat after costs — believe that number. Keep: the corpus decision, §0.2/0.3 protocols, Sleeve A meta-labeling structure, Sleeve B's 09:35-entry gap regime classifier (as raw material for the merged gap sleeve), the two-rule baseline null for Sleeve B.

Correct strategic framing (concede everything faster than minutes; live in the 30min-hours band) and the best deployment sequencing of the four: Sleeve 1 (ETF intraday momentum, Gao et al.) is buildable in under a week on a fixed 27-ETF universe with no survivorship issues, auction exits via cls orders, and a tiny meta-filter — it is the right first-live sleeve to prove the whole pipeline even though its economic ceiling is 2-6% CAGR contribution on ~half-hour-per-day exposure. The auction-order doctrine (opg/cls fills at SIP prints, sidestepping IEX entirely) and the pre-registered 2x-cost gates are excellent and should propagate to every other design. Sharpest criticisms: (1) Feasibility error — 'IEX minute bars for 600 symbols is within free-tier websocket limits' is almost certainly false; Alpaca's free plan caps websocket subscriptions at ~30 symbols. Sleeve 3 as written does not run; it is salvageable only via dynamic subscription (subscribe on news trigger, ~10-25 events/day) and Sleeve 2's 09:30-09:35 feature window needs REST-snapshot polling instead of streaming. This must be re-probed before any build. (2) Sleeve 1's edge is public since 2018 and post-publication replications show roughly half the original effect concentrated in high-VIX regimes; the 2022-2025-subsample gate is the right test but expect it to barely pass or fail — treat this sleeve as infrastructure with option value, not a return engine. (3) Sleeve 3 carries a self-assessed 40-50% death probability and duplicates design 2's Sleeve A with worse corpus discipline; two teams should not build the same intraday news-drift trade. (4) Per-trade net edge of 2-4bps on Sleeve 1 means one bad fill assumption erases the strategy — the live fill-vs-model reconciliation is not optional. Keep: Sleeve 1 as first deployment, the auction execution doctrine, the ±30s/±5bps jitter-test design rule, the shadow-mode latency reconciliation gate (best idea in the document, applies to every news-triggered sleeve), Sleeve 2's opening-window spread estimation via Corwin-Schultz.

Part B is the best portfolio-level engineering in the whole exercise — virtual sub-account ledgers, intent-based OMS with netting and internal crossing, hard pre-trade risk limits, fail-closed data-quality gates, ERC allocation with a clipped Hedge overlay explicitly rejecting Kelly on noise — this is the skeleton the combined system should run inside, and it matches the account owner's existing fail-closed philosophy. Sharpest criticisms: (1) S1 gives up the best part of the reversal trade by entering next morning 09:35-09:45: a large fraction of short-term reversal realizes overnight, and design 1's XSR entering near the close captures it; S1 as specified is a strictly weaker cousin of XSR and should be merged into it (its genuinely good ideas — candidate-gating, correlation-based sector assignment, sector-hedged residual labels — become XSR features, not a separate sleeve). (2) The unsupervised layers (Isolation Forest gate, k-means clusters, HMM) add three more fitted objects and hence silent degrees of freedom while being sold as 'not overfittable'; iforest-top-decile ∧ resid_z>2 needs an ablation showing iforest adds anything over the plain z-score gate, else it is complexity cosplay. (3) S3's tradable leg (QQQ/IWM/RSP/IEF/GLD/BIL rotation) duplicates what the owner's existing bot already does with seven sleeves and has nothing to do with irregularity exploitation — ship the HMM as a monitoring/gating overlay only, exactly per its own ≥0.1-Sharpe-improvement gate. (4) Trade frequency (6-16 orders/day S1, 0-5 S2) is adequate but the 30-40 engineering-day path before first fills is the slowest of the four; the OMS should be built minimal (netting + hard limits) and grown, not perfected upfront. (5) S2's pre-open IEX quote for gap estimation is the shakiest data dependency anywhere in the four docs — pre-market IEX is thin; the decision-noise simulation and staleness auto-disable are the right mitigations and must be kept. Keep: Part B nearly wholesale, S2's OPG auction execution + decision-noise backtest technique, HMM overlay (monitoring-only), the kill-criteria-as-design-artifact culture.
